name: Alloderm lip augmentation

lead: AlloDerm lip augmentation uses processed donor dermis from cadavers, with living cells removed, to add volume to the lips. Surgeons place it in small rolls in the lip to add size, or along the lip border to sharpen the edge, according to Wikipedia. The added volume is visible once healed.
A 2000 paper in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery is titled "Alloderm lip augmentation", but its abstract was not available, and no outcome data were found in the sources reviewed.

paras: Rolled or layered donor dermal tissue is inserted into the lip mucosa to add bulk, or into the vermilion border to define it. It is a surgical procedure done by a surgeon.
No specific complication data for this use were found. Wikipedia lists general lip augmentation complications such as swelling, bruising, asymmetry and lumpiness.

angle.text: Processed donor skin is placed in small rolls in the lip to add size, or along the lip border to sharpen it, giving fuller or crisper-edged lips. The added volume is visible once healed. Sources describe it briefly, with one 2000 paper title.

lead: AlloDerm lip augmentation uses processed donor (cadaver) dermis, with living cells removed, to add volume or definition to the lips. Wikipedia says it is placed under local anesthesia in small rolls in the mucosa to increase lip size, or in the vermilion to sharpen the border of the lip.[1] People choose it for fuller or better-defined lips that last longer than a temporary filler, because the graft is tissue rather than a gel that is absorbed within months.[1]

A 2000 letter titled "Alloderm lip augmentation" by J. M. Gryskiewicz appeared in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery as a comment on an earlier article.[2] A 2020 case report in Eplasty described using AlloDerm together with a local advancement flap for lip augmentation in a musician.[3] A 2024 claims analysis of 431 US adults found AlloDerm used mainly in oral cavity reconstruction, septal repair and rhinoplasty, and parotidectomy, with reoperation within 30 days in under 1 percent; its authors were affiliated with the product's maker.[4]

Wikipedia groups AlloDerm with other lip options including injectable fillers and implant strips such as expanded PTFE, and lists risks common to lip augmentation such as swelling, bruising, asymmetry and implant extrusion.[1] No comparative trial of AlloDerm for lip augmentation was located.
infobox: AbbVie, per authors of a 2024 study[4]

paras: The material is human dermis processed to remove viable cells and used as a graft.[1] Wikipedia describes two placements in lip work: rolls inside the mucosa for volume and a strip at the vermilion to define the lip edge. It does not give a duration for the result.[1]

Wikipedia lists other lip options: expanded PTFE implant strips, which can shift or extrude; permanent fillers such as PMMA microsphere products, which can form nodules and are generally avoided in the lip body; and hyaluronic and other fillers, with overfilling producing an exaggerated look and uneven results producing lumpiness or ridges. Common reactions include redness, swelling, bruising and uneven lips, lasting several days to a week, and smoking slows healing.[1]

No studies found of AlloDerm for lip augmentation beyond a 2000 letter without an abstract and a 2020 single case report describing AlloDerm with an advancement flap.[2][3] A 2024 claims analysis of AlloDerm in head and neck procedures did not focus on lips.[4]

timeline.event: "Alloderm lip augmentation" letter by Gryskiewicz is published in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery.[2]
Eplasty case report describes AlloDerm with a local advancement flap for lip augmentation.[3]
